question: Should a video document show the Library in the dock without being asked?
context: The Library shelf now holds a video document's recordings and sounds, and a tile drags onto a track. It is hidden until View > Library, because of your note that the Library would almost never be used. The video mock keeps it in the dock.

options.label: Show it, folded, for video
options.summary: Any document with a timeline shows the Library header at the bottom of the dock, folded. One click opens the shelf with your clips. Pictures keep it hidden until View > Library.
pros: Matches the video mock: the media pool is one click away
A Premiere editor finds their bin without hunting through the View menu
cons: One more header in a dock that is already long on a recording
options.mitigation: It sits folded at the bottom, so it costs one row until opened.

options.label: Show it open for video
options.summary: A document with a timeline shows the Library open, tiles and all, the moment it opens.
pros: Your clips are visible straight away, nothing to click
cons: Pushes the other sections down on every recording, even when you only want to trim one clip
options.mitigation: The shelf remembers if you fold it.

options.label: Keep it behind View > Library
options.summary: Nothing changes: the Library appears only after View > Library, for pictures and video alike.
pros: The dock stays as short as it is today
cons: Someone who knows Premiere will not find the bin, and dragging a clip off it is how the mock starts a project
options.mitigation: A hint on the empty timeline could point at View > Library.
